items.title: Specification / notes
items.text: The property is 100 ft wide (street side, south) by 140 ft deep. The dashed red rectangle on the plan is the property line. Two-story house with an attached garage on the east side; the house is beige siding with a dark gray roof. Keep it simple for this first test: transcribe the house, driveway, front walk, lawns, beds and all plants shown in the legend.

items.title: Answers to round 1 questions
items.text: Yes, the garage is a two-car garage facing the street (south). Yes, the three gray circles in the front tree bed are boulders. Location: Columbus, Ohio (lat 39.96, lon -83.0, UTC-4 in summer); north is up on the plan. There is a 6 ft wood privacy fence along the back and both sides of the backyard, from the back corners of the house to the rear property line. Please run the validate and check commands this time and confirm the overlay lines up.

rounds.summary: Revised the design file for the 100 ft x 140 ft lot: a two-story beige house with a dark gray hip roof, an attached east garage, driveway, curved front walk, stoop, flagstone patio with seat wall and stepping stones, two lawns, six beds, three boulders, and all legend plants (about 80 plants across 14 species). Added street, front-walk, backyard, aerial, top, orbit and flythrough views, and calibrated the plan image on the two property-line corners.
notes: I could not run ./lv validate or ./lv check (command execution was not approved in this session), so the design is NOT verified against the plan overlay. Please run both and look at the check image.
The plan looks like a render of the bundled demo design, so I transcribed positions from that design, which matches the plan's pixel layout, rather than measuring them independently.
plan.image points at app/files/d15bc71b47/landscape-plan.png, not an imported copy under plan/ (the plan/ folder is empty).
Calibration uses the NW and SE corners of the dashed red property line: (602,66) = (0,140) and (1273,1005) = (100,0).

Estimated, not on the plan: house wall height 19 ft, garage wall height 10 ft, roof types and pitches, window and door placement, bed edging and surface materials, flagstone/bluestone/concrete paving materials, and the seat wall height.
Terrain is flat and the site location is a placeholder (lat 40, lon -83).
Boulders (3) are included because gray circles appear in the tree bed, though they are not in the legend.
Public sidewalk is drawn south of the property line; the street itself is not modeled.
questions: Is the garage a two-car garage facing the street (south), as drawn?
Are the three gray circles in the front tree bed boulders?
What are the actual site address/latitude, so the sun angle is right?
Is there any fence on the property line? None is shown on the plan.

issues.message: 2 plant(s) outside the property boundary: street-tree-e, street-tree-w

rounds.summary: Revised the Elm Street Test design: the site location is now Columbus, OH (lat 39.96, lon -83.0, UTC-4), and I added a 6 ft wood privacy fence along the west side, across the rear and along the east side of the backyard. The two-car street-facing garage door and the three boulders in the front tree bed were already modeled that way, so they are unchanged. `./lv validate` reports no errors, and the `./lv check` overlay lines up with the plan: house, garage, driveway, walk, patio, beds and plants all sit on the drawing.
notes: The fence runs on the property lines: x=0 from y=77 to the rear, across y=140, and x=100 from y=72 (the garage's back corner) to the rear. Its start points are the back corners of the house/garage measured in y, but the fence sits on the property line, not against the house.
The short gap between the house and each side fence (west: x 0 to 25 at y=77; east: x 97 to 100 at y=72) is left open. Add return fence sections or gates if they exist.
The fence is modeled as 6 ft privacy style with the default wood color.
Validate warns that the two street trees (street-tree-w, street-tree-e) have their centers outside the property boundary, in the street strip. That matches the plan, so it is intentional.
The plan image is a rendering with the same legend plants as the model, so plant positions were kept from round 1. The property-line calibration corners are unchanged.
questions: Are there gates in the privacy fence, for example on the side yards beside the house?
Should the fence be closed back to the house on each side (west at x=25 and east at the garage)?
